config.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Go/no-go for the Aurora mobile app launch

personas.name: Isabel
personas.role: VP of guest experience, chairs the meeting
personas.hidden_agenda: The CEO mentioned the app in an investor call

personas.name: Femi
personas.goals: Launch without the key problems coming back
personas.hidden_agenda: The lock vendor's SDK is still a black box to his team

personas.name: Gwen
personas.hidden_agenda: Two general managers told her they don't want the app

personas.name: Rahul
personas.goals: Make sure the numbers are read correctly
personas.hidden_agenda: Found that the success rate drops at night

agenda.title: Pilot results
agenda.goal: Review the mobile check-in and digital key pilot

agenda.title: Hotel readiness
agenda.goal: Confirm the front desks are ready

agenda.title: Launch call
agenda.goal: Decide on June 10 and the rollout order

facts.statement: Average time saved per check-in = 6 minutes

beats.summary: Results; Isabel rounds up the success rate; Femi lowballs key failures and is corrected later
Front desk readiness; Gwen's training number stands
The pen test; one owner, one wobble

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Thanks for joining. Let's start with the pilot. The headline is a ninety-eight percent check-in success rate, which is fantastic.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: The dashboard says ninety-two. Ninety-eight was the success rate at the iOS hotels only.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Ninety-two, then. Still good.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: It is. It drops at night, though. After eleven it's closer to eighty-five.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: That's when the night auditor is alone at the desk. Exactly when you don't want failures.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: The night drop is the lock vendor's server doing maintenance. We've asked them to move it.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: How many check-ins was the pilot in total?

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Forty-three fifty, across seven hotels.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: And the time saved?

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Six minutes per check-in on average.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: Six minutes for the guest. Not for the desk when it goes wrong.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: What about the digital keys?

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: Key failures are under one percent now. Much better than in March.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Good. Guests rated the pilot four point six, which is the highest we've had for anything.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: Guests who got in. The ones who didn't call the front desk.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Support calls were one point eight per hundred check-ins.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: That's lower than the old kiosk.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: Hang on. I have the incident log from the Seaport hotel open. Key failures there were three and a half percent last month, not under one.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: Three point five across the chain, yes. Under one was the target after the firmware update, which isn't out yet.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Then the firmware update matters for the launch.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: It does.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Hotel readiness. Gwen?

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: We've trained about a hundred front desk staff so far.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Out of how many hotels?

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: Thirty-eight in the chain, but we'd start with the bigger ones.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: What do the desk staff do when a digital key fails?

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: They cut a plastic key, like always. That part's easy. It's the queue that's the problem.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Did anyone watch the finale last night? I'm still upset.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: Don't. I haven't seen it yet. I'm watching tonight.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: I stopped after the season with the twins. It got silly.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Okay. Could we have a manager on duty at the desk for the first week at each hotel?

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: For the big ones, yes. For the small ones, it's one person at night anyway.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Then the first week has a manager on the desk at every hotel with more than two hundred rooms.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: I'll send the general managers a staffing note on Monday.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: Has anyone asked the night auditors what they think of it?

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Two general managers have said they don't want the app at all. Is that a problem?

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: It's a conversation. Not a problem yet.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Security. Femi, the pen test.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: Two medium findings are still open. Both are in the key-sharing feature.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Can we launch with them open?

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: I'd rather not. If we turn key sharing off at launch, both findings go away.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: Guests won't miss key sharing. Most don't know it exists.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Then key sharing is off at launch, and we turn it on when the two findings are closed.

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: I'll get the flag set and ask the testers to confirm the findings are out of scope.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: It'd be worth someone checking how many pilot guests actually used key sharing.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Rahul, you'd know better than anyone. Could you pull that number?

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Sure. By tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: The call. Are we launching on June tenth?

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: Only if the firmware update is out. The key failures need to come down first.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: And not at the two hotels whose managers said no. Not yet.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Then June tenth, conditional on the firmware, starting with the twelve biggest hotels. The rest follow in July.

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: Should we email the loyalty members? That's two hundred and ten thousand people.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Not on day one. Let's see the first two weeks before we tell everyone.

turns.speaker: Gwen
turns.text: Who tells the CEO it's conditional?

turns.speaker: Femi
turns.text: When does the lock vendor ship the firmware? Do we have a date?

turns.speaker: Rahul
turns.text: They said the first week of June. They also said April.

turns.speaker: Isabel
turns.text: Thank you, everyone. We'll check in on the firmware next Friday.
